mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility over the last two weeks, reaching over 20% above baseline at t-0w, indicates a general increase in outdoor activity and willingness to leave home, which will spill over into retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility remains high or increases further, but the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w, increasing by 14.9 points from t-1w's low of -39.9%, suggests a return to office and associated weekday retail activity, which will boost RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 10 points week-on-week from a value below -30%
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility rebounds as specified, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not show an increase compared to the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and strong rebound in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w indicates a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting patterns and associated out-of-home activities, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility rebound at t-0w, but the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility to below 4% at t-0w, following a period of higher values, indicates people are spending less time at home and more time out, which directly benefits RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 4%, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases or remains flat compared to the previous 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The strong rebound in GROCERY_PHARM mobility at t-0w, reaching -2.3% from a low of -8.4% at t-1w, suggests increased general out-of-home activity and consumer confidence, which will positively influence RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases at t-0w, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not show an increase compared to the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC at t-0w (4.3 points) from a low point at t-1w indicates a turning point in consumer behavior, leading to further increases in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 points week-on-week, but then declines in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility over the last two weeks coupled with a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility at t-0w implies a strong shift towards more outdoor and out-of-home activities, which will eventually include retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility increases and RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases, but the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility, after its recent rebound, falls by more than 5 points week-on-week in the near future, it signals renewed caution or tightening of public health policies, which would negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility falls by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days remains stable or increases compared to the previous 14 days.
